title: Navigation priority matrix and compact switch (WIP)
summary: Working notes on a compact left-nav + quick-switch pattern, plus a prioritization matrix for routing surface area. Purpose: reduce cognitive load for power users while keeping discoverability for new users. This doc collects wireframe observations, microinteraction sketches, route mapping, and backlog tasks for implementation/testing.
wireframe_notes: High-level sketches included in attachments (see linked PR for demo slot). Key screens: 1) Collapsed global rail with icon-only primary nav + hover peek; 2) Quick-switch modal (Cmd-K style) that surfaces routes, resources (models, deployments, rollouts), and recent searches; 3) Top contextual bar that shows route breadcrumbs and rollouts toggle. Notes: prefer 24px icon grid, 56px collapsed rail width, 240px expanded panel. Keep primary actions (Create, Deploy, Monitor) pinned to top-level zones for muscle memory.
nav_principles:
- Prioritize task completion: top-level nav reflects high-frequency tasks (routes derived from telemetry).
- Progressive disclosure: collapsed rail + quick-switch + contextual breadcrumbs reduce permanent complexity.
- Deep-linkability: every view should be addressable (full URL + hash for sub-tabs) for SSO links, support, and tooling.
- Role-aware visibility: hide admin-only routes for non-admins to reduce clutter.
- Predictable fallbacks: if model variant missing, route should show fallback CTA rather than 404.
- Accessibility: keyboard-first quick-switch, focus traps for modals, ARIA labels on expanded states.
- Performance: avoid route-level bundle splitting that adds >100ms to cold nav transitions.
route_prioritization_matrix:
Columns: Route / Weekly uniques / Average session depth / Business criticality / Complexity to implement / Priority (1-5). Example rows (abbrev):
- Deployments: 6.5kWU / depth 3.2 / critical / complexity 3 / priority 5
- Models catalog: 4.2kWU / depth 2.1 / high / complexity 2 / priority 4
- Observability (console traces): 3.0kWU / depth 4.5 / high / complexity 4 / priority 4
- Billing: 1.1kWU / depth 1.4 / medium / complexity 2 / priority 2
Decision: show high priority (4-5) as top-level hubs, medium as nested, low in utility menu. Use matrix to drive what appears in collapsed rail vs quick-switch suggestions.
microinteractions_and_specs:
- Hover peek: delay 160ms to open preview, 120ms to close when mouse leaves.
- Quick-switch: keyboard shortcut Cmd/Ctrl+K, typeahead with fuzzy matching, show top 5 recents at top. Hit Enter to navigate; Shift+Enter opens in new tab.
- Breadcrumbs: clickable segments; when route has >4 segments collapse middle into chevron menu.
- Animation: use 150ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1) for rail expansion to feel snappy.
- Telemetry: emit nav_event with attributes {from_route,to_route,trigger} for every navigation; sample rate 1% for high-volume flows initially.
access_and_permissions_notes:
- Route-level guards: enforce server-side checks and mirror in UI by hiding actions rather than showing disabled states (reduces accidental click confusion).
- Audit links: any route exposing rollout/keys must include 'View audit log' CTA for enterprise plan.
- Role matrix: show admin-only nav items only when user.roles contains admin or infra. Edge-case: user with SSO-groups not fetched yet should see a temporary skeleton instead of full nav to avoid flash of privileged items.

decisions:
- Move Observability and Deployments to top-level hubs (priority 5).
- Use collapsed left rail as default for new users; onboarding modal introduces quick-switch and top-level hubs.
- Implement quick-switch before full rail refactor to unblock power users.
- Use path-based routing (no hash) for primary pages; reserve hash fragments for in-page tabs to keep server routing stable.
open_questions: Should collapsed rail be default for mobile/tablet sizes or should we surface a bottom nav for mobile?
How do we treat third-party plugin links (should they be pinned in top-level or Utility menu)?
What is the expected performance budget for first nav transition on cold load for Dedicated customers?
Do we surface deprecated routes in quick-switch results with a deprecation flag?
